body:
## Problem

id(web/image-upload): the image upload flow shape-trusts the `/api/upload` response — a wrong-shape 200 response silently inserts an image node with `src: undefined` (or a numeric `src`) into the document, and a `null` body is misreported as an insertion failure for an upload that "succeeded".

`pkgs/id/web/src/image-upload.ts`:

- `:109` — `return (await response.json()) as UploadResponse;` in `uploadImageFile()` is a bare cast; any 200 body is resolved as a well-formed `{ hash: string; name: string; url: string }` with no validation. The `!response.ok` guard at `:104` only covers non-200 statuses.
- `:277-283` — the caller (`handleImageUpload`) treats any resolution as success (`outcome.ok = true`); only a rejection takes the upload-failure path.
- `:312-315` — on "success" the caller creates the image node with `src: outcome.result.url` and `alt: outcome.result.name || fileName`. With a wrong-shape body, `result.url` is `undefined`, so a src-less image node is inserted into the real document and dispatched. With a `null` body, `result.url` throws a raw `TypeError` inside the insertion `try`, which the catch at `:320-328` reports as "Insertion failed" — the wrong diagnosis (the upload response was malformed; nothing about the document insertion was at fault), and the placeholder is removed with no accurate feedback anywhere.
- A wrong-typed body is worse: `{ url: 123 }` inserts an image node with `src: 123`.

The server contract is three required strings (`pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:1564` `UploadResponse { hash: String, name: String, url: String }`, returned at `:2226`), so a wrong-shape 200 requires deploy skew, a proxy/error envelope with a 200, or a future contract change — exactly the boundary this cast refuses to check. Siblings: #7812 (image-browser `/api/images`, same src-less-insert outcome via a different module), #7811 (home feed).

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop @ origin/main af4e603e89, image-upload.ts md5 41fa9f0a3ba46a56452fd5c3608fef75)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-upload-shape/probe.ts` (bun, real module imported from a clean `git archive origin/main` snapshot at `~/git/fleet/probe-main-c`, fetch stubbed per case; caller effect mirrors `image-upload.ts:312-315`):

- control (well-formed `{hash:"abc123", name:"cat.png", url:"/blob/abc123?filename=cat.png"}`): resolves the object — image node attrs `src="/blob/abc123?filename=cat.png"`, `alt="cat.png"` — OK
- `null` body: RESOLVES `null` (not rejected) → caller deref throws `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'result.url')`, caught and misreported as "Insertion failed"
- `{}` body: resolves `{}` → image node created with `src=undefined`
- `"abc"` body: resolves `"abc"` → image node created with `src=undefined`
- `[]` body: resolves `[]` → image node created with `src=undefined`
- `{hash:42, name:null, url:123}`: resolves → image node created with `src=123`
- `{hash:"abc123", name:"cat.png"}` (missing `url`): resolves → image node created with `src=undefined`

The existing tests (`pkgs/id/web/src/image-upload.test.ts`, `uploadImageFile` describe at `:231`) mock only the well-formed success body, a non-ok response, and a network error — no malformed-200 cases.

## Why it matters

Paste/drop image upload is a primary editing path. The upload itself succeeded server-side (the blob is stored), so a wrong-shape response today either corrupts the document with a broken src-less image node that then gets saved, or misdiagnoses the failure as an insertion problem — making the real contract break undebuggable from user reports. Failing closed is cheap: validate the shape at the fetch boundary and let the existing upload-failure path (warn + placeholder removal, `:279-282`) handle it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A malformed `/api/upload` 200 payload (null/non-object body, missing `hash`/`name`/`url`, or wrong-typed fields) makes `uploadImageFile` REJECT with a clear upload error — it never resolves a malformed value.
- [ ] On a malformed payload, no image node is inserted, and the failure is reported through the existing upload-failure path ("Upload failed for …"), never as "Insertion failed" and never as a raw TypeError.
- [ ] Well-formed payloads behave exactly as today (existing `uploadImageFile` tests unchanged and green).
- [ ] New regression tests in `pkgs/id/web/src/image-upload.test.ts` cover the malformed cases above and fail pre-fix.
- [ ] Web suite + typecheck green.
